note: SAMPLE starter curriculum. Generic practice only. Every module imports as Draft and must be reviewed by a trainer before approval.

modules.title: Working safely around AV gear
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Why safety habits come first: cables, power, lifting and keeping walkways clear.

skills.name: Routes or covers a cable so that it is not a trip hazard in a walkway
Reports a damaged cable or plug to a trainer instead of using it
Lifts and carries a heavy case using a safe technique or asks for help
Identifies where the nearest power isolation and first-aid point are in the room

questions.prompt: A cable has to cross a walkway during an event. What is the best approach?
options: Leave it loose so it is easy to move later
Tape one end only and hope people notice
Cover it with proper cable protection and mark it so people can see it
Run it across and ask people to step carefully

questions.prompt: You notice a power lead with a cracked outer sleeve. What should you do?
options: Wrap it with tape and keep using it
Take it out of use, label it as faulty and tell a trainer
Use it only for small items
Put it back in the box without saying anything

questions.prompt: A case is too heavy to lift comfortably alone. What should you do?
options: Lift it quickly to get it over with
Ask for a second person or use a trolley
Lift it by the handle with a twisting motion

questions.prompt: Why should you know where power isolation points are before an event?
options: So you can reset the equipment during a show
So you can reduce the electricity bill
So you can borrow power for personal devices
So power can be switched off quickly in an emergency

questions.prompt: Which is the safest way to unplug a mains lead?
options: Twist the cable until it comes free
Hold the plug body and pull it out, not the cable
Use pliers to grip the plug

modules.title: Signal flow: source to speaker or screen
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. The idea that every signal travels from a source, through processing, to an output, and how to trace it.

skills.name: Names the main stages a signal passes through in a simple audio system, in order
Names the main stages a signal passes through in a simple video system, in order
Traces a signal from a microphone to a loudspeaker by physically following the cables
Explains in their own words why a fault can be anywhere along the chain

questions.prompt: In a simple audio system, which order is correct?
What is the main benefit of understanding signal flow when something stops working?
options: You can avoid ever having faults
You can skip testing before an event
You can replace all the equipment straight away
You can check one stage at a time instead of guessing

questions.prompt: A microphone is a typical example of which part of the chain?
A projector or screen is a typical example of which part of the chain?
If there is no sound from one microphone but others work, where is it sensible to look first?
options: At the loudspeakers used by every channel
At the power supply for the whole building
At the screen showing the slides
At the stages that only that microphone uses, such as its cable and channel

modules.title: Labelling and cable handling
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Keeping kit identifiable and tidy: labels, coiling, storage and why it saves time.

skills.name: Coils a cable using a consistent method that avoids twisting and kinks
Applies a clear label to a cable or case following the team convention
Returns equipment to its labelled storage place after use
Checks a cable visually for damage before connecting it

questions.prompt: Why do teams label cables and cases?
options: So items can be identified quickly and returned to the right place
To make the kit look more expensive
Labels are only needed for new kit

questions.prompt: What is a good reason to coil cables the same way every time?
options: It prevents kinks and makes them quick to deploy
It improves the signal on every cable

questions.prompt: What should you do before plugging in a cable?
options: Bend it sharply to test it
Plug in both ends before looking
Look along it and at both connectors for visible damage

questions.prompt: After an event you find a case with no label. What is the best action?
options: Ask a trainer and label it following the team convention
Put it with any other case

questions.prompt: A cable has been left in a tight knot. What is the best way to deal with it?
options: Pull hard until it comes apart
Gently undo the knot, then coil it properly

modules.title: Communicating as part of a crew
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Clear, calm communication during setup and events: asking, confirming and reporting.

skills.name: Repeats back an instruction to confirm it was understood
Uses agreed terms for locations and equipment when speaking to the crew
Tells the team lead promptly when something is not working
Asks a question when unsure instead of guessing

questions.prompt: A team lead gives you an instruction you do not fully understand. What should you do?
options: Ask for it to be explained again before acting
Guess and hope it is right
Do something similar that you already know

questions.prompt: Why is repeating back an instruction useful?
options: It confirms that both people understood the same thing
It slows people down on purpose
It shows you are more senior
It is only needed for written instructions

questions.prompt: You spot a problem during setup. What is the best action?
options: Fix it quietly and say nothing
Wait until the end of the event
Tell the team lead clearly and promptly

questions.prompt: Why do crews agree common names for places and equipment?
options: So everyone means the same thing when they speak

questions.prompt: During a live event, which style of speech is most helpful?
options: Loud and urgent for every issue

modules.title: Load-in, setup and strike
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. The sequence of setting up before an event and packing away after it, with checklists.

skills.name: Follows a setup checklist in order and ticks items as completed
Positions equipment according to the plan or lead instruction
Runs and secures cables so they are safe and tidy
Carries out a strike so that nothing is left behind and everything is stored
Reports missing or damaged items at the end of strike

questions.prompt: Why use a checklist for setup?
options: It replaces the need to understand the system
It reduces the chance of missing a step

questions.prompt: What is a sensible order for strike?
options: Power down, disconnect, coil and pack, then check the room
Pack the cases first, then switch off
Leave the cables out until the next day

questions.prompt: At the end of strike you notice a cable is missing. What should you do?
options: Replace it with a personal cable
Tell the team lead so it can be found or recorded

questions.prompt: Why should equipment be powered down before disconnecting it?
options: To protect people and the equipment from avoidable faults
Because the cables are easier to coil

questions.prompt: What does a good last check of the room involve?
options: Looking for left-behind items, tape, waste and open cases
Checking only that the doors are open

modules.title: Audio basics: gain and monitoring
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Setting a healthy input level, listening in headphones and keeping the mix clean.

skills.name: Sets the input gain of a channel so the signal is strong without distorting
Uses headphones to check a source before sending it to the room
Mutes unused channels
Explains the difference between gain and fader level in their own words
Recognises distortion by ear and by the meters and reduces the level

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of setting input gain?
options: To make the channel permanently louder than the others
To add reverb to the sound
To change the colour of the sound
To give the mixer a healthy signal level without distortion

questions.prompt: What should you do if a channel meter is constantly in the red?
options: Reduce the gain until the signal is no longer clipping
Ignore it if the sound seems fine

questions.prompt: Why mute channels that are not in use?
options: It saves the microphones from wear
It makes the mixer start faster
Muted channels cannot be heard even after unmuting
It reduces noise and the risk of unwanted sound

questions.prompt: Which best describes the difference between gain and the fader?
options: Gain sets the level coming in; the fader sets the level going on to the mix
They are the same control with different names
The fader changes the cable type

questions.prompt: Why use headphones when checking a source?
options: To hear it before it reaches the audience
To block the room noise forever
It is required by law for every source

modules.title: Video basics: sources, displays and matching
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. How computers and cameras connect to displays, and why the right settings matter.

skills.name: Connects a laptop to a display using the correct cable and adapter
Confirms that the display is on the correct input
Adjusts the output settings so the image fills the screen correctly
Checks that a presentation appears correctly before the audience arrives

questions.prompt: A display shows no picture. What is a sensible first check?
options: That it is switched on and set to the correct input

questions.prompt: Why should you test a presentation before the audience arrives?
options: To find and fix problems while there is time
Testing is only needed for audio

questions.prompt: An image looks stretched. What is the most likely area to check?
options: The output and display aspect settings

questions.prompt: What is an adapter used for in a video connection?
options: To supply power to the room
To connect two different types of connector

questions.prompt: A laptop does not send a picture to the display. What should you check on the laptop?
options: Whether the keyboard has a label
Whether it is set to use the external display

modules.title: Batteries, wireless and spares
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Looking after battery powered items and having what you need on hand.

skills.name: Checks the battery level of a wireless item before use
Replaces or charges batteries following the team routine
Stores batteries safely and separate from damaged ones
Keeps a basic spares kit stocked and tells the lead when something runs low

questions.prompt: When should battery levels be checked?
options: Before the event and at agreed points during it
Only at the end of the year

questions.prompt: What should you do with a battery that looks swollen or damaged?
options: Stop using it, keep it apart and tell a trainer
Put it back in the box
Use it for a short time only
Throw it in a general bin without telling anyone

questions.prompt: Why keep a spares kit?
options: So common problems can be fixed quickly

questions.prompt: What is the best way to know when spares are running low?
options: Check the kit regularly and report shortages
Wait until a spare is needed

questions.prompt: Why should used and fresh batteries be kept separate?
options: They do not fit in the same box
So you do not accidentally put weak ones into equipment

modules.title: Running audio for a simple event
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Operating a small mix under supervision from soundcheck to the end of the event.

skills.name: Carries out a line check of each source before the event
Sets an initial balance so speech is clear and comfortable
Adjusts levels during the event in response to changes
Recovers calmly from a problem and tells the supervisor what happened
Brings the system down at the end in the agreed order

questions.prompt: What is the aim of a line check?
options: To reduce the number of channels
To confirm that each source reaches the mix correctly

questions.prompt: During the event a speaker moves further from the microphone and gets quieter. What is a sensible response?
options: Raise the level smoothly and tell the speaker if needed

questions.prompt: A loud noise suddenly appears. What is the best first action?
options: Wait to see if it stops
Turn the master fader to maximum
Quickly identify the source and reduce or mute it

questions.prompt: Why tell your supervisor about a problem even after you fixed it?
options: So the team can learn and prevent it happening again

questions.prompt: What does a good balance for speech aim for?
options: Quiet enough that nobody can hear
Clear and easy to understand at a comfortable level

modules.title: Camera and vision mixing basics
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Framing, switching and handing over shots calmly for a simple live event.

skills.name: Frames a shot of a speaker that is steady and appropriate
Checks focus and exposure before the event
Switches between sources at sensible moments with a clean transition
Follows the director or lead instruction using agreed calls

questions.prompt: Why check focus and exposure before the event?
options: So the picture is usable from the start

questions.prompt: What is a good habit when switching shots?
options: Switch to a ready, stable shot without hurried changes
Switch constantly to keep it interesting
Switch to a shot while it is still being adjusted

questions.prompt: A camera operator is asked to "hold" a shot. What does this most likely mean?
options: Keep the framing steady until told otherwise

questions.prompt: Why use agreed calls between operators?
options: To make the event feel formal
So everyone understands instructions the first time
So only one person can speak

questions.prompt: A shot is slightly tilted. What should the operator do?
options: Level the camera and tell the lead if needed

modules.title: Presentation and playback operation
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Running slides, video and music cues on time with backups ready.

skills.name: Loads the presentation or media and confirms it plays correctly before the event
Follows a cue sheet and plays items on cue
Keeps a backup copy of the media accessible
Communicates with the speaker about how slides will be controlled

questions.prompt: Why keep a backup copy of media?
options: Because backups make the file bigger
So you can recover quickly if the main copy fails

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a cue sheet?
options: To list what happens and when so everyone follows the same plan

questions.prompt: Before the event you load a video and it does not play. What should you do?
options: Wait to see if it plays during the event
Fix or replace it before the event, and tell the lead

questions.prompt: A speaker asks to change slides themselves. What is a good response?
options: Agree how it will work and confirm it before the event

questions.prompt: Why check the media in the actual room setup?
options: Conditions in the room can differ from your desk

modules.title: A method for troubleshooting
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. A calm, repeatable way to find faults: observe, isolate, test one change at a time and record.

skills.name: States the symptom clearly before changing anything
Narrows the problem to one part of the signal chain
Changes one thing at a time and checks the result
Restores anything they changed that did not help
Records what was found and fixed

questions.prompt: What is the best first step when something stops working?
options: Clearly describe what is and is not working
Blame the last person who used it

questions.prompt: Why change only one thing at a time?
options: So you know which change made the difference
It is quicker to do ten things at once

questions.prompt: You swap a cable and the fault is still there. What should you do?
options: Put the original cable back and test the next stage

questions.prompt: What does it mean to isolate a fault?
options: Narrow it to the smallest part of the system that can explain it

questions.prompt: Why record what you found and fixed?
options: So others can fix it faster next time

modules.title: Pre-event checks and show readiness
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Preparing a complete system so that it is ready before people arrive.

skills.name: Completes a full pre-event check against the checklist
Tests every signal path that will be used, including backups
Confirms with the event owner what is needed and when
Identifies and resolves risks before the doors open

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a pre-event check?
options: To fill the time before the event
To find problems before the audience is present

questions.prompt: Why test backup paths as well as the main ones?
options: A backup that has never been tested may not work when needed

questions.prompt: What is a good reason to talk to the event owner before setup?
options: To make sure you prepare what they actually need

questions.prompt: You find a risk that cannot be fixed before the event. What should you do?
options: Tell the lead and agree a plan or workaround

questions.prompt: When should the final check be completed?
options: Early enough to leave time to fix anything found

modules.title: Fault-finding under time pressure
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Applying a troubleshooting method calmly when the event is live.

skills.name: Stays calm and communicates status to the lead during a fault
Prioritises quick checks that are most likely to help first
Switches to a prepared workaround to protect the audience experience
Documents the fault after the event and follows it up

questions.prompt: During a live fault, what should be your priority?
options: Protect what the audience sees and hears while you work out the cause

questions.prompt: Why start with the quick, likely checks?
options: They resolve many faults with the least disruption

questions.prompt: What does a workaround do?
options: Keeps the event going while the real cause is fixed later
Removes the need for a record

questions.prompt: Why tell the lead what is happening during a fault?
options: So decisions can be made with the whole picture
So someone else can take over the blame

questions.prompt: After the event the fault is still unexplained. What should you do?
options: Wait for it to happen again
Record it and follow it up so it does not repeat

modules.title: Records and handover
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Leaving clear notes so the next person can pick up where you left off.

skills.name: Writes an event report that states what happened and what to follow up
Records equipment issues with enough detail to act on
Hands over to the next shift with a clear verbal and written summary
Keeps labels and records up to date after changes

questions.prompt: What makes a good issue report?
options: Only the name of the person who found it
Clear symptoms, where and when it happened, and what was tried
A long story with no details

questions.prompt: Why hand over in writing as well as verbally?
options: So nothing is lost if someone forgets
It is optional and rarely helpful

questions.prompt: You change how a system is connected. What should you also do?
options: Nothing, people will work it out
Update labels and records to match

questions.prompt: What should an event report highlight?
options: What went well, what went wrong and what needs follow-up

questions.prompt: Why keep records up to date?
options: Out-of-date records mislead people and cause mistakes

modules.title: Leading a crew during an event
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Briefing, assigning roles, keeping the crew calm and making decisions in real time.

skills.name: Gives a clear pre-event briefing covering roles, plan and contingencies
Assigns tasks according to the skill level of each crew member
Keeps a calm communication tone during problems
Makes and communicates a clear decision when options are uncertain
Leads a short review after the event

questions.prompt: What should a good briefing cover?
options: Roles, the plan and what to do if something goes wrong

questions.prompt: How should tasks be assigned?
options: All to the most senior person
According to the person's skill and supervision needs
To the person who speaks the most

questions.prompt: A problem occurs during the event. How should a leader speak?
Why hold a short review after an event?
options: To learn what to keep and what to change

questions.prompt: A decision has to be made without full information. What is a sensible approach?
options: Choose the safest workable option and tell the crew why
Let the crew vote on every choice

modules.title: Coaching and assessing a trainee
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Teaching a skill, observing fairly, giving useful feedback and recording evidence.

skills.name: Demonstrates a skill step by step, then lets the trainee try
Observes a trainee practising without taking over unless safety requires
Gives specific feedback that names what was done well and what to change
Scores the trainee against the rubric using what was actually observed
Records a short note that describes the evidence for the score

questions.prompt: What is a good way to teach a new skill?
options: Show it, explain it, then let the trainee try with support
Let them work it out alone

questions.prompt: When should an assessor step in during a practical?
options: When there is a safety risk or the trainee asks for help

questions.prompt: Which is the most useful feedback?
options: Specific comments about what was done and what to change

questions.prompt: On what should a practical score be based?
options: How long they have been on the team
What the assessor actually observed in the task

questions.prompt: Why write a short evidence note with a score?
options: So the score can be understood and trusted later

modules.title: Reviewing and improving the system
modules.summary: SAMPLE – review before use. Looking at how the team and equipment are set up, spotting weak points and managing change safely.

skills.name: Reviews a system diagram and identifies a single point of failure
Proposes a change with the reason, risks and a way to undo it
Tests a change outside a live event before using it live
Updates documentation and training material when something changes

questions.prompt: What is a single point of failure?
options: A part that is never used
One part whose failure would stop the whole system

questions.prompt: Why include a way to undo a change?
options: So the team can return to a working state if the change goes badly
It makes the change slower for no reason

questions.prompt: Where is it best to test a change first?
options: Only on the day it is needed
Outside a live event, in a safe setting

questions.prompt: When equipment or process changes, what else should change?
Why explain the reason for a change to the team?
options: So people understand and use it correctly
